Strict blocking, explained

The best strict app blockers for iPhone

A strict label is not enough. Compare what happens when you try to edit the rule, leave early, delete the app, disable Screen Time access, or handle a genuine exception.

By Hussain TaheriLast checked August 31, 202612 minute read

Publisher disclosure: Twilock publishes this page. We compare products against their official pages and help documentation, include drawbacks, and link the sources so you can verify the details yourself.

Direct answer: Choose Twilock for strict Night and Morning windows, Opal for a polished multi-rule system with a documented weekly Emergency Pass, Jomo for highly configurable strict sessions, one sec for strict blocks plus interventions, ScreenZen for free strict controls, and Freedom when cross-device locked sessions matter most.

What “strict” should mean

Strictness has several layers. A product can prevent an early exit but still let you edit a future schedule. It can protect a rule inside the app while leaving the Screen Time permission exposed in Settings. It can prevent uninstalling itself while still offering an emergency path.

Before enabling any strict mode, check five things:

  1. Can the active rule be edited or deleted?
  2. Can the session end early?
  3. What happens if you try to delete the blocker?
  4. Can Screen Time permission be disabled?
  5. What is the emergency or recovery path?

1. Twilock — strict protection around sleep

Twilock

Best for: strict Night and Morning windows

Twilock’s Strict Mode is part of Pro and is tied to its focused schedule model. The live App Store listing says it stops you deleting Twilock mid-session while always leaving a way out.

Advantages: Very clear use case, minimal schedule complexity, active uninstall protection, and lower current U.S. pricing than several premium competitors.

Drawbacks: Only two window types, a two-hour cap per window, iPhone only, and Strict Mode is not in the free tier.

Choose it if: your main bypass happens at bedtime or on waking and you do not want a general-purpose rule engine.

2. Opal — strictness inside a broad system

Opal

Best for: many strict rule types

Opal’s Pro Hard Mode can run with No Unblocks, preventing an early exit or edit. Its official help center documents one Emergency Pass each week, plus additional steps for uninstall and Screen Time protection.

Advantages: Clear emergency policy, flexible Schedules and Sessions, multiple rule types, Allow Only, and cross-platform support.

Drawbacks: Higher current web price, more setup, and some foolproof configurations require additional iOS settings.

Choose it if: you need strict rules for work, study, bedtime, app opens, and usage limits in one product.

3. Jomo — strict rules with the most knobs

Jomo

Best for: custom strict sessions and unlocks

Jomo’s official features page describes Strict Mode as making rules unbreakable so they cannot be deleted or bypassed. Its help center also documents the iOS limitations and extra Settings/Shortcuts setup that can strengthen protection.

Advantages: Many rule types and unlock actions, solid current annual price, iPhone and Mac support, and rich customization.

Drawbacks: The number of options takes more learning, and the strongest Settings protection may require extra setup outside Jomo.

Choose it if: you want to design your own strict system and care more about flexibility than minimalism.

4. one sec — strict blocks plus opening interventions

one sec

Best for: strict sessions and app-opening friction

one sec Pro offers Strict Block Sessions and recurring blocks. Its current guide says a strict block cannot be paused or left before the time ends, and its iOS 26.4 documentation describes locking Screen Time permission with a code.

Advantages: Combines strict blocking with the app-opening intervention that made one sec distinctive; supports scheduled blocks and multiple platforms.

Drawbacks: Strict sessions and unlimited apps require Pro, and features differ by platform.

Choose it if: you want both hard blocks and a daily pause that interrupts automatic app opens.

5. ScreenZen — best free strict option

ScreenZen

Best for: strict controls without a subscription

ScreenZen’s site describes a lock mode that protects common loopholes and can prevent uninstalling, while the App Store listing documents strict blocks for time ranges, open counts, or Screen Time.

Advantages: Free and donation-supported, highly configurable, broad platform support, and no Pro gate for core strict tools.

Drawbacks: More configuration than a focused schedule and less concise public documentation about one universal emergency model.

Choose it if: you want the strongest free feature set and are comfortable tuning it yourself.

6. Freedom — best for locked sessions across devices

Freedom

Best for: cross-device sessions

Freedom Premium adds scheduling, recurring sessions, longer sessions, and Locked Mode. One account can include iPhone, Android, Mac, Windows, and Chromebook in the same blocking system.

Advantages: Excellent platform coverage, cross-device sync, website and app blocking, and a lifetime plan.

Drawbacks: Its strict story is centered on not quitting a session, not a narrow iPhone bedtime commitment, and Premium is required for Locked Mode and recurring schedules.

Choose it if: the loophole is switching from your phone to a computer when a block starts.

Choose by the loophole you actually use

Choose Twilock if…

  • You delete or edit the blocker during a bedtime window.
  • You only need Night and Morning.
  • You want a clear recovery path rather than a sprawling settings system.

Choose an alternative if…

  • Opal: many strict rule types and a documented weekly pass.
  • Jomo: deep custom rules and unlocks.
  • one sec: strict blocks plus interventions.
  • ScreenZen: free strict controls.
  • Freedom: cross-device locked sessions.

Methodology

We reviewed official product pages and help documentation for active-rule editing, early exit, emergency access, uninstall or permission protection, schedule flexibility, platform support, and current pricing. We did not assign a universal “hardest to bypass” winner because iOS version, Screen Time configuration, Family Sharing, and each user’s chosen escape path materially change the result.

Frequently asked questions

Can an iPhone app blocker be impossible to bypass?
No honest comparison should promise that in every setup. iOS permissions, device version, passcodes, Family Sharing, emergency paths, and physical access all matter. Aim for enough friction to interrupt your own common bypass.
What is the best free strict app blocker?
ScreenZen offers the clearest free strict-blocking feature set in this group. Apple Screen Time with a passcode can also be effective, especially when another trusted person controls the code.
Should strict mode have an emergency exit?
That is a personal trade-off. A recovery path reduces the risk of being locked out of something genuinely needed; a faster exit also becomes a loophole. Read the exact behavior and test a short block first.
Can a strict blocker stop me deleting it?
Some products document uninstall protection in certain modes or iOS configurations. Twilock specifically says Strict Mode stops deletion mid-session. ScreenZen, Opal, Jomo, and one sec document additional protection paths with varying setup.
